mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, or SPX posts negative 60-day returns in > 40% of quarters with accelerating GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM manufacturing index (proxied by INDPRO) falls below 50 for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in industrial activity that will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 50 for 2 months, or INDPRO mean-reverts above 50 within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.5 percentage points over 3 months signals a rapidly weakening labor market, which will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending slows.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, or UNRATE falls back below its 3-month-ago level within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise by more than 10% year-over-year while the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 4%, it signals a strong housing-led economic expansion that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where HOUST YoY > 10% and FEDFUNDS < 4%, or FEDFUNDS rises above 4% within the next 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 2% over 3 months signals a surge in inflation that will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the Fed tightens monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 2% in 3 months, or CPIAUCSL falls back below its 3-month-ago level within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) is growing by more than 200,000 per month, it signals a tight labor market that will lead to wage inflation and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS growth > 200k per month
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS growth > 200k, or UNRATE rises above 4% within the next 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) rises by more than 5% year-over-year while the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3%, it signals a strong manufacturing-led expansion that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances where INDPRO YoY > 5% and FEDFUNDS < 3%, or FEDFUNDS rises above 3% within the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 5% month-over-month signals a sudden weakening in consumer demand that will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS drops > 5% MoM, or RSAFS rebounds by more than 3% within the next 2 months.
